          type: string

## Summary

I implemented the `sharesHousehold` / `householdId` feature for `POST /api/owners`. The Cp10 duplicate-household rejection (with the `sharesHousehold` opt-out) was already present; the missing piece was assigning and returning a stable shared `householdId`.

Changes:

- **`src/main/resources/openapi.yml`** — added a `householdId` (readOnly string) property to the `Owner` response schema, so the generated `OwnerDto` gains the field.
- **`model/Owner.java`** — added the `householdId` field (`@Column(name = "household_id")`) with getter/setter. MapStruct auto-maps it into `OwnerDto`.
- **`db/{hsqldb,h2,mysql,postgres}/schema.sql`** — added the `household_id` column (tests run with `ddl-auto=none`, so the schema is script-driven).
- **`rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — added `householdIdFor(lastName, address)`, which derives the id deterministically as upper-case hex of SHA-256 over the *collapsed* last name + address (the same normalization used by the existing duplicate-household check), and assigns it in `addOwner`.

Because the id is a pure function of the household's last name and address, every owner in the same household — the original owner and any later joiners created with `sharesHousehold: true` — receives the identical, non-blank identifier without needing to read any other owner's value. That satisfies Cp11 (joiners share the same `householdId`) while Cp10's rejection/opt-in behavior is unchanged.

All 21 tests pass (`BUILD SUCCESS`).
